cards.front: What should you know about class in "jekyll and hyde"?
cards.back: Jekyll is respectable middle-class professional; Hyde represents the underclass he secretly joins. Class boundaries are both rigid and permeable.

cards.front: What should you know about effect on structure?
cards.back: Dickens's novels have cliffhangers at chapter ends because they were originally published in parts. Each installment needed to keep readers hooked.

cards.front: What should you know about ao3 context strategy?
cards.back: For the 19th century novel question, AO3 is worth 25% of marks (typically 8 out of 30 marks). Spend roughly 5-7 minutes of a 45-minute response on embedding context. Never bolt context on at the end — weave it into your argument. Examiners reward contextual points that illuminate the text, not historical facts listed for their own sake. A Grade 9 response treats context as the lens through which the text's meaning becomes clear, not a separate paragraph tagged on as an afterthought.

cards.back: Anonymity in cities (e.g. Stevenson's anonymous London)

Factory owners, professionals (e.g. New money, respectability, morality)
Factory workers, servants (e.g. Poverty, hard labour, no vote)
Criminals, beggars (e.g. Desperate, invisible to society)
